territorial_scope.description: Governs exports from the United States to the People's Republic of China and defines persons to include entities wherever located.

evidence.quote: any individual, corporation, partnership, association, or other legal entity, wherever located

summary.short: Bars any person from exporting, reexporting or transferring an advanced AI semiconductor to the People's Republic of China unless the Secretary of Commerce approves the transfer and Congress enacts a joint resolution approving it. The Act sunsets three years after enactment.
summary.long: The bill would prohibit any person from exporting, reexporting or transferring an advanced AI semiconductor to the People's Republic of China unless the Secretary of Commerce has approved the transfer after an interagency review and Congress has enacted a joint resolution specifically approving it. An advanced AI semiconductor is one that exceeds any of four thresholds: total processing performance of 2,400 or performance density of 1.6, DRAM bandwidth above 4,100 GB/s, interconnect bandwidth above 1,100 GB/s, or combined DRAM and interconnect bandwidth above 5,100 GB/s. The People's Republic of China includes Hong Kong, Macau and entities owned or controlled by its government or the Chinese Communist Party. The Secretary must submit a report to Congress within 30 days of a determination. Exceptions cover humanitarian exports, exports needed for U.S. diplomatic or consular facilities in China, and returns for repair or replacement of chips lawfully exported before enactment. The Act ceases to be effective three years after enactment. The text contains no penalty provisions and no separate enforcement authority.

relations.note: Sec. 2(b)(1) defines 'intelligence community' by reference to section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947. The bill does not reproduce that definition.

notes: Bill as introduced; the document gives no effective date. Sec. 2(d)(3) and Sec. 4 refer to 'the effective date of this Act' without setting one. Sec. 3(1) says a semiconductor 'exceeds any of the following thresholds', but clause (A) uses 'or more' ('a performance density of 1.6 or more') while clauses (B) to (D) use 'exceeding'; the operators are inconsistent and are coded as written. No legal basis, amendments or repeals are stated.
